subject: Async switchover RPO waiver discussion with Meridian Payments
messages:
From: Meredith Haynes <meredith@meridian-payments.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: async switchover RPO waiver for Meridian production

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Meridian's platform team dug the low-latency results. We have one operational constraint that will affect the failover guarantees: our payments ledger uses a cross-region eventual-replication layer (async) for cost reasons. During a region switchover, not all ledger rows converge instantly.

We'd like to request a temporary exception in the Redwood SLA for the Meridian account for multi-region failover: specifically, allowance for an RPO of up to 2 hours for non-reconciled ledger rows during an async switchover, and an activation lead time (pre-warm window) of 30 minutes for our standby region. Procurement wants this documented as part of the SOW.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept that carve-out (we're happy to subscribe to additional monitoring and incident playbook requirements)? If not, what mitigations or commercial terms would you propose?

Meredith Haynes
Head of Platform Operations, Meridian Payments
meredith@meridian-payments.com

Attachments: meridian-async-switchover-req-20281120.pdf (PDF)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: async switchover RPO waiver for Meridian production

Hi Meredith — thanks for the clear write-up and the attachment. We're glad Meridian saw value in the demo.

Short answer: we can consider a scoped exception, but we need an internal risk assessment and a concrete mitigation plan before committing in the SOW. Next steps from our side:
- I'll loop in infra/eng for an assessment of the activation lead time and RPO exposure.
- Can you share any existing runbooks for your replication windows and the list of critical queues/keys that must be prioritised during switchover?
- We'll propose an SLO carve-out template (technical caveats + monitoring obligations) and share it back for Meridian legal/procurement review.

I'll have a proposed text and engineering guidance by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Nov 2028 11:49:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: async switchover RPO waiver for Meridian production

Quick technical readout from infra: here's what we're seeing and what we can offer as mitigations.

Summary of risk:
- Meridian's ledger topology (async cross-region replication) means write-to-primary may not be visible in standby until replication completes — so a strict RPO=0 guarantee can't be held for all keys.
- During switchover we can prioritize certain key namespaces to replicate first, but this requires agreement on which namespaces are "critical" and may incur additional CPU/bandwidth cost.

Potential compromise we can support:
1) Scoped SLO carve-out: allow RPO up to 2 hours for non-critical/bulk namespaces, provided Meridian implements per-namespace reconciliation hooks and agreed monitoring (error rates, replication lag metrics sent to our observability webhook).
2) Critical-path protection: Redwood to commit to <=30m RPO for up to N critical namespaces (N to be negotiated), using prioritized replication and prefix-level KV cache reconciliation. This will be an add-on in Dedicated/Private modes; for Hosted we can offer it as a paid service-tier with a config flag and additional throttling limits.
3) Activation window: 30-minute warmup is acceptable if Meridian performs pre-switchover validation and provides a signed runbook checklist to our ops team; otherwise we'd require 2-hour lead time for full warmup on shared capacity.

Operational guardrails required for any exception:
- Meridian must provide a list of critical namespaces and the reconciliation playbook.
- Telemetry: replication lag and reconciliation status must be published to the shared monitoring channel.
- Post-incident: Meridian must run the reconciliation playbook and provide Delta reports within 24 hours.

I'll draft SOW language for Marissa to review. If we move forward, finance/procurement should log the add-on as a recurring charge (to cover prioritized replication costs).

— Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, procurements@meridian-payments.com <procurements@meridian-payments.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Nov 2028 16:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: async switchover RPO waiver for Meridian production

Hi Meredith — thanks for the patience. Internal engineering reviewed the request and here's our proposed path forward for the SOW: 

Proposal (short form):
- Scoped carve-out: Redwood will permit an RPO up to 2 hours for non-critical namespaces during a multi-region async switchover.
- Critical-path commitment: Redwood will guarantee an RPO <=30 minutes for up to 8 critical namespaces, subject to configuration and additional service charges.
- Activation window: Redwood accepts a 30-minute pre-warm activation window provided Meridian delivers the signed switchover runbook checklist and performs the pre-switchover validation steps. Without the runbook, activation lead time reverts to 2 hours on shared capacity.
- Monitoring & post-incident: Meridian must provide reconciliation hooks and publish replication lag telemetry to our observability channel; Meridian will deliver a reconciliation report within 24 hours of any switchover event.

I've attached a one-page SOW fragment and a draft DocuSign link for quick signature: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/meridian-payments (proxy link for procurement). Attachments: redwood-failover-proposal-20281121.docx, meridian-async-switchover-req-20281120.pdf

If Meridian is comfortable, please reply with approval and procurement details and we'll route a finalized SOW through Legal.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Rachel — this looks reasonable and aligns with our risk profile. Meridian approves the proposed carve-out and critical-namespace approach; procurement will expect the SOW fragment and the DocuSign. We'll send our list of the 8 critical namespaces and the runbook checklist by EOD tomorrow.

Meredith Haynes
Head of Platform Operations, Meridian Payments
